brief: BTIG's Jonathan Krinsky presses his cautious refiners call, first made mid-September and reiterated mid-October, after the group's +157% YTD gain (best in three decades, nearly 2x the prior record) reversed with a 6.8% drop on Tuesday, the worst day since the April 2025 Liberation Day selloff. Unlike 2025, this drop started from record highs with the S&P up, which Krinsky reads as the start of an unwind rather than capitulation. The driver is margins: the 3-2-1 crack spread fell from a September peak near $70/bbl to about $51, multi-month lows, while refiner stocks kept climbing until about two weeks ago, so equities priced in margins just as they rolled over. Gasoline, two-thirds of the barrel, is the weak leg even as diesel stays in crisis. Krinsky links the refiner unwind to market-wide fragility: SPX price and breadth have diverged on 33% of 2026 trading days, the most since 1996, with energy acting as an offset whose removal could trigger the correlated-down day he has warned about since September. The article's own view sides with Krinsky: fundamentals (tight product market, outages beyond Goldman's worst case) can coexist with falling refiner shares because the 157% gain already discounts more than tightness.
